Welcome to Mossbourne Riverside Academy
At our academy, we hold a firm belief that all pupils can succeed when expectations are high, the learning environment is calm and purposeful, and every child is supported to reach their full potential.
Principal’s Welcome
We are proud to be part of Mossbourne Federation, a family of high-achieving academies rooted in the vision of Sir Clive Bourne to provide children in Hackney with an outstanding education.
At our academy, we hold a firm belief that all pupils can succeed when expectations are high, the learning environment is calm and purposeful, and every child is supported to reach their full potential.
In September 2016, our building opened on Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park. It is here, on this prestigious site, that we have expanded over the years to become a three-form entry primary academy, providing a happy, stimulating and caring place where dignity, respect and good behaviour underpin all aspects of daily life.
Our values of Excellence, No Excuses and Unity are lived out every day. We believe in doing everything as well as we can, persevering with determination, and working together with integrity and mutual support. We teach a balanced, knowledge-rich curriculum, designed to build deep understanding, resilience and creativity, preparing our pupils for future challenges and opportunities.
We are committed to nurturing well-rounded, confident learners who leave us ready to thrive academically and personally, so they can make their communities proud and fully prepared for the bright, successful future ahead of them.
I warmly welcome you to explore all that our academy offers.
Mossbourne Values: Excellence, Unity, and No Excuses
Being part of the Mossbourne Federation means joining a community defined by unapologetically high standards, ambition and a relentless commitment to excellence. We do not accept “good enough”; instead, we constantly push ourselves and others to ensure every student reaches their highest potential, never shying away from challenge or difficult truths.
Strive for excellence in all we do...
...excellence becomes both a habit and an expectation, with all students and staff supported to achieve the highest standards regardless of background or starting point.
Strive for unity in all we do...
...every student and staff member benefits from a shared mission, collective belief and a consistent world-class education.
Strive for a no excuses culture in all we do...
...barriers to learning are not accepted but addressed, enabling every student and staff member to achieve their full potential.

Mossbourne Community Academy began with a simple idea: Hackney children are as bright as children anywhere.
The issue was the schools and the too-low expectations of the people in charge, driven by unfounded assumptions about what Hackney children could achieve.
Over the last 20 years, Mossbourne Federation has influenced the quality of education received by children throughout England and beyond, still embodying the same principles set by its founder: outstanding quality of teaching and learning, with high expectations of every student.
2004
Founding Mossbourne Community Academy in 2004, the late Sir Clive Bourne made it his mission to provide Hackney children with a world-class education and drive the standards of educational provision in the borough.
This required Mossbourne to create an environment where teachers can teach and children can learn—that is, an environment where learning is the norm.
He believed that the children of Hackney were being incorrectly blamed for the failure of schools in the borough to reach good educational standards and that the real reasons lay elsewhere. “Good enough” was not a mantra he was prepared to put up with.
Sir Clive Bourne’s vision changed the face of education in Hackney.
Mossbourne Community Academy was not only one of the country’s first academies but the very first in Hackney, with the goal to re-imagine what inner-city, non-selective education could be. ​It showed everyone what was possible when the community focused on high-quality teaching and didn’t allow excuses, mediocrity and disruptive behaviour to get in the way.
2014-2016
With the opening of Mossbourne Victoria Park Academy in 2014, Mossbourne Parkside Academy in 2015 and Mossbourne Riverside Academy in 2016, Mossbourne Federation has come to provide a world-class education for children from 3 to 18 years old.​
2021
Under our guidance and driven by our shared ethos of excellence, unity and no excuses, Mossbourne Parkside Academy achieved its first ‘Good’ Ofsted judgment in 30 years.
2024
Following the merger with Ortu Trust in late 2024, Mossbourne Federation welcomed Mossbourne Port Side Academy, Mossbourne Fobbing Academy, Mossbourne Herd Lane Academy, and Mossbourne Sixth Form Thurrock into its growing family.
The merger was an opportunity for the Federation to extend beyond Hackney, delivering the same unwavering quality of teaching and learning.
After two decades of challenges and triumphs, Mossbourne continues its story of outstanding educational success, having grown to be one of the highest-achieving Multi Academy Trusts in the country.
100 Years, Not Tomorrow
For 20 years, we have been unapologetic in our ambitions.
We continue to break down barriers to education and break the mould. We are creating an environment where every child can excel, following the Mossbourne Mindset that keeps us working together to be truly exceptional.
Still, we believe that things that last a long time know how to move at an appropriate place.
Children get one chance at education and Mossbourne knows it. But we also know that if we are going to create meaningful change in the communities we serve, we need to think that the idea of Mossbourne is bigger than any of us.
This idea will and should outlive us, no matter the person in charge – we want it to survive forever and conserve its ethos as guardians, not owners.
It will take 100 years more for what we want to change in education to fully bear fruit, knowing that all the achievements of today, every Oxbridge admission, are just a part of the whole and an artefact of our enduring legacy.

The Mossbourne Curriculum:A Story of Excellence
Here at Mossbourne Federation, our curriculum is a carefully crafted story—one that transforms lives, builds character, and empowers pupils to write their own future. From the opening lines of early education to the final chapters of secondary school, every stage is designed with precision, ensuring that knowledge is gained, remembered, and applied with confidence.
Like the greatest stories, our curriculum is rich, sequenced with purpose, and grounded in the belief that every child can achieve excellence. It is knowledge-driven, shaped by cognitive science, and focused on deep understanding. We prioritise reading and language, knowing that words are the foundation of thought, opportunity, and social mobility. Through rigorous teaching and a culture of curiosity, we ensure that pupils not only acquire knowledge but retain and apply it, preparing them for the challenges ahead.
As pupils progress through each chapter of their education, they are challenged to think critically, communicate effectively, and embody the highest character. The Mossbourne curriculum extends beyond academics, offering experiences that build resilience, broaden perspectives, and cultivate a love of learning. Our values are woven into every lesson, interaction, and challenge— we actively develop pupils into thinkers, leaders, and creators who will shape the world beyond the classroom.
From mastering the foundations in primary to excelling in the EBacc subjects at secondary, every step of the Mossbourne journey is intentional, ambitious, and transformative. Pupils leave not just as learners but as authors of their own success, equipped with the knowledge, skills, and mindset to thrive.
Find out more about our curricula by clicking the links below.

Facilities Hire
Are you looking for the perfect venue for your next event, class or community activity? Mossbourne Federation offers a range of modern, well-maintained facilities available to hire outside of school hours at their academies based in Hackney and Thurrock.
Whether you are planning a sports session, a club meeting, a performance or a private function, our spaces provide a safe, welcoming and flexible environment for all kinds of occasions.

Independence and SEND at Mossbourne Federation
At Mossbourne Federation, we are committed to empowering every pupil, including those with special educational needs and disabilities, to reach their full potential.
Our approach to SEND is built on high aspirations and ambitious teaching that develops independence, resilience and the skills pupils need to thrive in their communities and lead fulfilling adult lives.
We recognise that SEND is diverse and complex, and we work hard to ensure every pupil can access the curriculum and the wider school life. The Federation supports a higher-than-average number of pupils with Education, Health and Care Plans, and we see this as central to who we are. We are proud of the role we play in providing inclusive, high-quality education.
Our Vision
The Mossbourne Federation is committed to fostering independent, confident, well-educated individuals who are passionate about learning. This objective equally applies to students with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
Always at the forefront of innovation in educational equality, the federation promotes independent learning and personal independence while actively discouraging dependency to forge confident, self-assured, and employable Mossbournians.
Rather than assigning one-to-one teaching assistants, we focus on enhancing the skills of ALL teachers to educate ALL students, in a way that is true to the exceptional teaching and learning approach that Mossbourne is known for.
Our belief is simple: all teachers are educators of SEND students and should be equipped with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to teach students with diverse needs in their classrooms.
SEND Support
The Federation employs specialist teachers who provide expert one-on-one and small group instruction for students with specific needs, such as dyslexia, ASD, or speech and language difficulties. The Federation regularly assesses the impact of SEND support and adjusts its practices according to each pupil's changing needs and progress.
Classroom instruction is supplemented by small group teaching and one-on-one lessons.
These sessions are used for intervention and developing skills to become independent, confident, well-educated citizens who love learning and will continue learning beyond their school years.
The Federation views SEND as an opportunity to create more effective and inclusive teaching and learning strategies that benefit all students.
Our ultimate goal is to enable pupils with SEND to become independent learners who can access the mainstream curriculum and participate fully in the school community, ensuring they can achieve the best personal and academic outcomes and life chances.
We adopt a child-centred approach that acknowledges the strengths and aspirations of each pupil. We believe that all learners should have the opportunity to follow the Mossbourne curriculum, which closely aligns with the national curriculum in primary and Key Stage 3 and sit a full suite of GCSEs in Key Stage 4.

Staff Culture
We firmly believe that a school is only as good as its people, and that the quality of a Trust’s teachers and support staff will always be reflected in the quality of teaching and learning.
Our staff strive towards a common goal: being the best we can be and ensuring every pupil, every teacher and every member of staff fulfils their potential. We value continuous improvement, are always learning, and always looking for a better way to do things.
We believe in doing what is right, as opposed to what is popular.
We are a supportive family that shares experiences, knowledge, and ideas in an environment that welcomes input and challenge.
Teachers and Support Staff
A Mossbourne member of staff will always display…
Alignment to the mission:
Changing children’s lives for the better by creating environments where learning is the norm.
Constantly striving to be better
Knowing that ‘good’ is not good enough
It is our belief that intellect, mission alignment and a Mossbourne Mindset cannot be taught, and we actively seek these characteristics when recruiting staff.
Leaders
A Mossbourne leader is always driven by these key characteristics…
Who am I?: They know who they are and continuously strive to know themselves better.
Mission: They believe in and live the mission.
Taking risks: They are always willing to take and celebrate measured risks.
Doing what is right: The will do what needs to be done regardless of the personal impact.
Growth mindset: They believe anything is possible. They are resilient, accepting challenges and knockback in their stride.
Teacher and learning: They are obsessed with teaching and learning, no matter their specialism.
Relationships: They understand that people work for people, seeking to form strong, respectful relationships.
We recruit all leaders to this ideal and know where their strengths and challenges lie, identifying opportunities for development at every stage.
We make no excuses for seeking these characteristics, because we know they are critical to us achieving our mission.

Safeguarding
The Mossbourne Federation is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and young people. We believe that every student has the right to feel safe, supported and valued within our schools, and we work tirelessly to create an environment where they can thrive both academically and personally.
Safeguarding is everyone's responsibility. Across the Federation, we maintain a strong culture of vigilance and care, ensuring that all staff, governors and volunteers understand their role in protecting children from harm. We take all concerns seriously and work closely with families, external agencies and partner organisations to ensure that students receive the support they need.
Our safeguarding practices are underpinned by statutory guidance and are regularly reviewed to ensure they remain effective and responsive to the needs of our communities.
Further information can be found in the policies and guidance documents below.
